comment: E1 cell map, Y3/Y4c/Y5/Y7 edition: every cell resolves to declared OpenGFX sprite ids (tools/opengfx-sprites.json, regenerated by `node tools/parse-pnml.mjs`) and every anchor is DERIVED from the declared xrel/yrel by the slicer — there are no hand-authored boxes, crops, tiles, compose blocks or anchors left in this file. Cell kinds: (a) plain declared ground tile (`sprite`, terrain_*); (b) `layers` — declared ground tile + declared building sprite(s) drawn at tileOrigin+(xrel,yrel), optional per-layer `tint` and `frames` for animation; (c) `trackset` — the 16 road/rail bitmask tiles built only from declared sprites (road = OpenGFX's finished flat tiles indexed through OpenTTD's flat table; rail = declared grass ground + declared rail overlay pieces); (d) `generator: highlight|highlight_soft|highlight_bad|node_mark` — the procedural placement glows (UI, not OpenGFX art): the solid placement tile, the fainter reach/catchment tint, the red invalid twin, and the thin neutral tag outline for tiles a placement qualifies or catches (PP-03). Building cells keep the gameplay footprint (catchment/occupancy); the sprite sits on the footprint's south tile by construction, which is what makes its base land inside the footprint diamond (Y7). MT-2: every industry is multi-tile — one cell per OpenTTD industry-tile type `m` (name `<key>_t<m>`), each drawing its declared ground + optional building at the declared xrel/yrel; the renderer emits one item per footprint tile (src/iso/renderer.ts) and src/iso/config.ts carries the same transcribed layout (the footprint stays the gameplay footprint). validate-manifest.mjs still fails a building sprite dramatically smaller than its footprint. Y8/T1: gold-mine tiles 72/74/75 (and their quarry twins) are single finished ground layers - 2247-2262 are ground tiles, not buildings. TOWN-3/Y8: towns use real house sprites transcribed from OpenTTD's _town_draw_tile_data complete stages (town_center = paved ground 1420 + hotel 1450; town_house_a/b/c = house/office/offices), replacing the coal-mine shed 2019 and the industries_misc 2180. T3/Y8: every factory_mt_* ground layer carries the same tintLum as its building, because industry_land.h colour-modifies the factory floor as well as the walls. PP-12: file cells pack standalone TTD building PNGs verbatim (src/assets/sprites/png/{industries,houses}/ttd/, the former assets/iso-ttd/): industries + factory as single auto-footprint sprites, resource-specific 1x1 Depots, the church town centre, one 1x1 town variant per remaining house file, and spare_-prefixed cells for art the game does not reference yet. Anchor = bottom-centre, footprint auto = square from art width (footprintForFileArt, mirrored by footprintForArt in src/iso/config.ts).

sprites.name: road
sprites.note: Y4c: OpenGFX ships the complete flat road set at 1332-1350 (straights, curves, T-junctions, crossroads — finished 64x31 tiles). Each of the 16 masks is converted to OpenTTD RoadBits (toOpenttdRoadBits, src/iso/track.ts) and indexes OpenTTD's flat selection table; the declared sprite is blitted verbatim. The generator is gone.

sprites.name: dirt
sprites.note: gravel: the basic road tier. OpenGFX has no gravel road art, so the 16 dirt_XXXX tiles come from the player-supplied recolor sheet (infrastructure/gravelroads.png): the finished flat road set recoloured to gravel, in the SAME mask order as the paved `road` trackset above (0..14 across the top row, the 4-way 1111 bottom-left), painted 2x. tools/slice-atlas.mjs makeGravelStrip slices each 128x64 source tile down to a 64x32 cell, so dirt tiles line up pixel-for-pixel with the paved Road tiles they upgrade to.
